CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.has_scope(tbl regclass) RETURNS boolean
  LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute a
                    WHERE a.attrelid = tbl AND a.attname = 'scope_id'
                      AND a.attnotnull AND NOT a.attisdropped)

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE public.rls_protect(tbl regclass)
  LANGUAGE plpgsql

  -- permanently. Without the pin the caller's search_path at CALL time decides
  -- which `current_scopes()` the floor calls, for the life of the policy.
  SET search_path = pg_catalog, public

  IF NOT public.has_scope(tbl) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION
      'rls_protect(%): scope_id must exist and be NOT NULL -- a NULL scope fails '
      '= ANY(), so the row is invisible to every role while the audit reports the '
      'table protected', tbl;
  END IF;
  EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %s ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', tbl);
  EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %s FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', tbl);
  EXECUTE format('DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenancy ON %s', tbl);

  EXECUTE format(
    'CREATE POLICY tenancy ON %s AS RESTRICTIVE FOR ALL '
    'USING (scope_id = ANY((SELECT current_scopes())::text[])) '
    'WITH CHECK (scope_id = ANY((SELECT current_scopes())::text[]))', tbl);
END $$;

-- A generated runtime can replace this transaction-entry hook to acquire its
-- write locks before table triggers (including IVM) acquire theirs.
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS mecha;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA mecha TO PUBLIC;
DO $init$ BEGIN
  IF to_regprocedure('mecha.request_write_gate()') IS NULL THEN
    EXECUTE 'CREATE FUNCTION mecha.request_write_gate() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $body$ BEGIN END $body$';

-- PostgREST calls this once per request, in the request's transaction, after
-- switching to the request role. It is what makes current_scopes() a constant
-- for the statement rather than a subquery per row.
--
-- A write to a table also names the transaction it runs in, as `x-txid`: the
-- client confirms the write by seeing that transaction in its shape stream,
-- and only this hook runs inside the transaction before PostgREST answers.
-- The id is the 32-bit xid, the form Electric reports a change's transaction
-- and a snapshot's bounds in; the 64-bit xid8 differs from it once the epoch
-- moves past 0. Not for a read, nor for a function call, which may be one:
-- naming a transaction assigns it an id, spent for nothing there. Added to
-- whatever headers the request already set rather than replacing them.
--
-- Every token the stack itself signs names its issuer, `mecha.stack_issuer()`
-- (services/auth/jwt.ts's STACK_ISSUER, the same value): the auth service's people and guests, the service token, the
-- edge's. The cluster's own roles, anon, app_user, service and any other it
-- holds, act only on such a token, and a role the app declared for another
-- issuer's tokens (`mecha.token_role`) only on one naming another issuer and
-- an audience (PostgREST checks an audience a token names against crud's, but
-- lets one naming none through, which would let a token minted for another
-- app sharing the issuer act here). A token naming no issuer is the stack's
-- from before it named one, believed only where the app trusts no other
-- issuer, so no outside key could have signed it; where it trusts one, such
-- a token acts as anon, with no subject: the request goes on as a reader
-- signed out, which the session it came from was not. The switch is allowed
-- because PostgREST's own role, the session's, holds anon. An outside
-- issuer's key that signs a token naming the stack's issuer is beyond this:
-- PostgREST does not say which key verified a token.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mecha.stack_issuer() RETURNS text
  LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE RETURN 'mecha:stack';
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION mecha.stack_issuer() TO PUBLIC;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.app_pre_request() RETURNS void
  LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$

  claims jsonb := coalesce(nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), ''), '{}')::jsonb;
  sub text := nullif(claims->>'sub', '');
  named boolean := claims ? 'iss';
  stack boolean := claims->>'iss' IS NOT DISTINCT FROM mecha.stack_issuer();
  audience boolean := CASE jsonb_typeof(claims->'aud')
    WHEN 'string' THEN claims->>'aud' <> ''
    WHEN 'array' THEN jsonb_array_length(claims->'aud') > 0

  -- (PGRST_APP_SETTINGS_TOKEN_ROLES), which PostgREST sets in every request
  -- and no client can: a role the registry still holds acts only while the
  -- deployment declares it, so one a release removed is refused from that
  -- release on, whether or not anything has pruned the registry yet. Unset,
  -- none is declared.
  declared text[] := array_remove(string_to_array(replace(coalesce(current_setting('app.settings.token_roles', true), ''), ' ', ''), ','), '');

  IF NOT named AND claims <> '{}'::jsonb AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM mecha.token_role) THEN

    -- Logged, the role alone and never the token, so a client still holding
    -- such a token is seen rather than silently signed out.
    IF current_user <> 'anon' THEN
      RAISE WARNING 'a token naming no issuer, as %, acts as anon where the app trusts another issuer', current_user;
      PERFORM set_config('role', 'anon', true);
    END IF;
    PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"role":"anon"}', true);
    sub := NULL;
  ELSIF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM mecha.token_role WHERE role_name = current_user) THEN
    IF current_user <> ALL (declared) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'a token acts as %, a token role this release does not declare', current_user
        USING ERRCODE = '42501';
    END IF;
    IF stack THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'a token acts as %, a declared token role, only as another issuer signed it', current_user
        USING ERRCODE = '42501';
    END IF;
    IF NOT audience THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'a token another issuer signed names no audience' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
    END IF;
  ELSIF named AND NOT stack THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'a token another issuer signed cannot act as %, which is no declared token role', current_user
      USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;
  IF sub LIKE '%,%' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'jwt sub contains a comma, which would split into two scopes';

    array_to_string(public.subject_scopes(sub), ','), true);

     AND current_setting('request.path', true) NOT LIKE '/rpc/%' THEN
    PERFORM set_config('response.headers',
      (coalesce(nullif(current_setting('response.headers', true), ''), '[]')::jsonb
        || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('x-txid', pg_current_xact_id()::xid::text)))::text, true);

-- Tables the floor cannot cover, declared rather than discovered.
--
-- A restrictive policy is tenancy isolation, and some visibility is finer than
-- tenancy: a per-object share grants one row to one reader, and there is no
-- scope both parties hold that does not also grant everything else the owner
-- has. Such a table is guarded by its permissive policies alone.
--
-- This exists so the audit can stay meaningful. Without it a sharing app's
-- audit is permanently non-empty, and a gate that always fails is one nobody
-- reads. Empty then means every table is either floored or knowingly exempt,
-- and `rls_exempt` is the short list a reviewer actually has to read.
-- Outside `public` on purpose. An app migration granting DML ON ALL TABLES IN
-- SCHEMA public -- an app's grants and publication do -- would otherwise
-- hand every signed-in user the ability to exempt any table and silence the
-- gate, and a REVOKE here would be undone by the next such grant. Being outside
-- `public` also keeps it off PostgREST, which serves that schema.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mecha.rls_exempt (
  table_name text PRIMARY KEY,
  reason     text NOT NULL
);
GRANT SELECT ON mecha.rls_exempt TO PUBLIC;

-- Where a shape may be keyed besides `scope_id`, declared rather than
-- discovered. A row of `table_name` keyed by `column_name` has the visibility
-- of the `parent` row that column names: a composition's rows are content of
-- their parent. Declaring the edge is what makes a per-object shape
-- (`note_item where note_id = '<row>'`) authorizable at all: the gate cannot
-- prove from a policy that every present and future row under a key is
-- readable, but an app that emitted the policy can say so, once, here.
--
-- `parent = 'subject'` is the one edge that names no table: the keyed rows
-- are addressed to a subject -- a grant table by its sharee column -- and the
-- value must be the caller. Not `app_user` by its key, which would make the
-- edge as wide as that table's policy, and an app may make app_user public.
--
-- Outside `public` for the reason given at `rls_exempt`: a row here widens
-- what a shape may carry, and an app grant must not be able to add one.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mecha.shape_key (
  table_name  text NOT NULL,
  column_name text NOT NULL,
  parent      text NOT NULL,
  parent_key  text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (table_name, column_name)
);
GRANT SELECT ON mecha.shape_key TO PUBLIC;

-- The roles a token another issuer signed may act as, declared rather than
-- discovered: the app's own, which its schema names here, and none of the
-- cluster's. Outside `public` for the reason given at `rls_exempt`: a row here
-- lets an outside issuer's token through `app_pre_request`. The row '', which
-- names no role, is an app that trusted an issuer once and declares none now:
-- a token naming no issuer stays anon's there.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mecha.token_role (
  role_name text PRIMARY KEY
);
GRANT SELECT ON mecha.token_role TO PUBLIC;

-- A composition's scope is its parent's, and a generated column cannot reach
-- another table, so this trigger writes it and overwrites anything supplied.
-- BEFORE, so the value is in the row Postgres stores; on UPDATE too, because
-- re-pointing the parent key is a move. Arguments: parent table, parent key,
-- the child's column naming it. The child's value is cast to the parent
-- key's type, so the lookup is the parent key's index.
--
-- A child of no parent has no scope. Where the column is a foreign key the
-- key refuses it, and this raises the same violation first, since NOT NULL
-- would otherwise answer before the key does. Where it is not -- a sink a
-- pipeline writes for a row that may since be gone -- the row is derived
-- data of nothing and is not stored, so the batch it came in lands.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mecha.scope_from_parent() RETURNS trigger
  LANGUAGE plpgsql
  SET search_path = pg_catalog, public
  AS $$
DECLARE
  ty text;
BEGIN
  SELECT format_type(a.atttypid, a.atttypmod) INTO ty FROM pg_attribute a
    WHERE a.attrelid = TG_ARGV[0]::regclass AND a.attname = TG_ARGV[1] AND NOT a.attisdropped;
  EXECUTE format('SELECT p.scope_id FROM %s p WHERE p.%I = ($1).%I::%s',
                 TG_ARGV[0]::regclass, TG_ARGV[1], TG_ARGV[2], ty)
    INTO NEW.scope_id USING NEW;
  IF NEW.scope_id IS NULL THEN
    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint c
                WHERE c.conrelid = TG_RELID AND c.contype = 'f'
                  AND c.conkey = ARRAY[(SELECT attnum FROM pg_attribute
                                         WHERE attrelid = TG_RELID AND attname = TG_ARGV[2])]) THEN
      RAISE foreign_key_violation USING MESSAGE =
        format('Key is not present in table "%s".', TG_ARGV[0]);
    END IF;
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

-- Whether a shape over `tbl` keyed `col = val` reaches only rows the caller
-- may read: the edge is declared, and the caller can read the parent row.
-- Evaluated as the caller, and it has to be: the gatekeeper sets the
-- subject's role and claims on its transaction first, so the SELECT on the
-- parent is the app's own policies answering -- the one derivation the CRUD
-- path reads. Not SECURITY DEFINER, which Postgres forbids from switching
-- role, and which would answer as its owner anyway.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mecha.shape_reach(tbl text, col text, val text) RETURNS boolean
  LANGUAGE plpgsql STABLE
  SET search_path = pg_catalog, public
  AS $$
DECLARE
  p text;
  k text;
  ty text;
  ok boolean;
BEGIN
  SELECT parent, parent_key INTO p, k FROM mecha.shape_key
    WHERE table_name = tbl AND column_name = col;
  IF p IS NULL THEN RETURN false; END IF;
  IF p = 'subject' THEN
    RETURN val = nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true)::json->>'sub', '');
  END IF;
  -- The value is cast to the key's own type, so the comparison can use the
  -- key's index; comparing on the text side would scan the parent per mint.
  -- A value the type will not take -- unparseable, out of range -- names no
  -- row: data_exception is the whole class.
  SELECT format_type(a.atttypid, a.atttypmod) INTO ty FROM pg_attribute a
    WHERE a.attrelid = p::regclass AND a.attname = k AND NOT a.attisdropped;
  IF ty IS NULL THEN RETURN false; END IF;
  BEGIN
    EXECUTE format('SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM %s WHERE %I = $1::%s)', p::regclass, k, ty)
      INTO ok USING val;
  EXCEPTION WHEN data_exception THEN
    RETURN false;
  END;
  RETURN ok;
END $$;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION mecha.shape_reach(text, text, text) TO PUBLIC;

-- It reads the catalog rather than the source because a hand-written migration
-- can bypass a generator and cannot bypass this. Every term rejects an object
-- that some earlier version of this called protected, and each is held down by
-- its own assertion. None is decoration; do not simplify one away.
--
-- A function rather than a bare view because `pg_get_expr` renders according to
-- the CALLER's search_path. Unpinned, an auditor with a different one gets false
-- failures, and -- worse -- a policy calling a wide-open `current_scopes()` from
-- another schema on the path renders bare and reads as protected.
--
-- Views and matviews are included because migrations run as the superuser, so
-- every object is superuser-owned: a view without `security_invoker` executes as
-- its owner and bypasses RLS, and a matview is a stored snapshot RLS never
-- evaluates at all. One CREATE VIEW would otherwise defeat the floor silently.
-- Outside `public` for the reason given at `rls_exempt`, and with more to lose:
-- this list names every table the floor does not cover.
--
-- Two drops with different jobs, neither redundant: the unqualified pair clears
-- the objects from `public` in a database created while they lived there; the
-- qualified one is what lets the file be applied to a database that already has
-- it, which is how a correction to the floor reaches one.
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.rls_unprotected;
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.rls_audit();
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS mecha.rls_unprotected;
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mecha.rls_audit()
  RETURNS TABLE (table_name text, reason text)
  LANGUAGE sql STABLE
  SET search_path = pg_catalog, public
AS $$
  SELECT n.nspname || '.' || c.relname,
         CASE c.relkind
           WHEN 'm' THEN 'materialized view: a snapshot RLS never evaluates'
           WHEN 'v' THEN 'view without security_invoker: runs as its owner'
           ELSE CASE
             WHEN NOT c.relrowsecurity      THEN 'RLS not enabled'
             WHEN NOT c.relforcerowsecurity THEN 'RLS not forced: the owner is exempt'
             WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_policy p
                           WHERE p.polrelid = c.oid AND p.polpermissive
                             AND p.polroles = '{0}'::oid[])
               THEN 'a permissive policy granted to PUBLIC: every role holds public:, so anon reaches what it admits'
             ELSE 'no tenancy policy: restrictive, PUBLIC, FOR ALL, both sides the scope test'
           END
         END
    FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
   WHERE c.relkind IN ('r', 'p', 'v', 'm')
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM mecha.rls_exempt e
                      WHERE e.table_name = n.nspname || '.' || c.relname)
     AND n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema', 'pg_toast')
     AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg\_temp\_%'
     AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg\_toast\_temp\_%'
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_depend d
                      WHERE d.objid = c.oid AND d.classid = 'pg_class'::regclass
                        AND d.deptype = 'e')
     AND (c.relkind = 'm'
          OR (c.relkind = 'v'
              AND NOT coalesce(c.reloptions, '{}') @> ARRAY['security_invoker=true'])
          OR (c.relkind IN ('r', 'p')
              AND (NOT c.relrowsecurity
                   OR NOT c.relforcerowsecurity
                   OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_policy p
                               WHERE p.polrelid = c.oid AND p.polpermissive
                                 AND p.polroles = '{0}'::oid[])
                   OR NOT EXISTS (
                        SELECT 1 FROM pg_policy p
                         WHERE p.polrelid = c.oid
                           AND NOT p.polpermissive
                           AND p.polroles = '{0}'::oid[]
                           AND p.polcmd = '*'
                           AND pg_get_expr(p.polqual, p.polrelid)
                                 = '(scope_id = ANY (( SELECT current_scopes() AS current_scopes)::text[]))'
                           AND pg_get_expr(p.polwithcheck, p.polrelid)
                                 = '(scope_id = ANY (( SELECT current_scopes() AS current_scopes)::text[]))'))))
$$;

-- security_invoker because the audit flags views that lack it, and a check that
-- exempts itself is not one. It runs as the reader either way: rls_audit reads
-- only catalogs.
CREATE VIEW mecha.rls_unprotected WITH (security_invoker = true)
  AS SELECT * FROM mecha.rls_audit();

-- A function is EXECUTE TO PUBLIC by default, so the schema move alone would
-- leave the view denied and the function under it callable by anyone. Both
-- surfaces or neither: assertions 39 and 40. `rls_exempt` is readable by
-- contrast because a GRANT says so.
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION mecha.rls_audit() FROM PUBLIC;

-- `rls_exempt` is a table in a schema the audit scans, so it exempts itself
-- -- by a row, in the list a reviewer reads, rather than by a term in the
-- predicate where nobody would find it.
INSERT INTO mecha.rls_exempt VALUES
  ('mecha.rls_exempt', 'the exemption list: readable by all, writable by none'),
  ('mecha.shape_key', 'the shape edges: readable by all, writable by none'),
  ('mecha.token_role', 'the roles an outside issuer''s token may act as: readable by all, writable by none')
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

-- The request a transaction serves, carried through CDC: the change feed's
-- rows carry no session state, so the W3C traceparent of whoever wrote them
-- is written into the WAL as a row of its own. The generator of a feed's
-- publication puts this table in it, and a statement trigger calling
-- mark_txn() on every table it publishes; pgoutput's protocol 1 sends a
-- transaction whole, so the marker reaches a consumer immediately before the
-- transaction's first change. A transaction with no trace still gets one, so
-- a consumer can tell where each transaction starts. bigint and not xid8: the
-- WAL reader resolves no xid8 field type.
--
-- Append-only, about 120 bytes per writing transaction with its key: a delete
-- would reach the feed as a change every consumer must filter. Partitioning
-- by time and dropping old partitions bounds it without a word on the feed.
--
-- It lives here because this is the one step the image restates ahead of any
-- caller step, and the publication naming it is a caller step.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mecha.txn_trace (
  txid        bigint PRIMARY KEY,
  traceparent text NOT NULL,
  at          timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- A writer outside PostgREST states its trace by SET LOCAL mecha.traceparent;
-- PostgREST's own request headers answer otherwise. A value that is not a
-- version-00-shaped traceparent is no trace, as W3C Trace Context says a
-- receiver treats one: the header is the client's to send.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mecha.traceparent() RETURNS text
  LANGUAGE sql STABLE
  SET search_path = pg_catalog
  AS $$
    SELECT coalesce(substring(
      coalesce(nullif(current_setting('mecha.traceparent', true), ''),
               nullif(current_setting('request.headers', true), '')::json->>'traceparent')
      FROM '^[0-9a-f]{2}-[0-9a-f]{32}-[0-9a-f]{16}-[0-9a-f]{2}$'), '')
  $$;

-- BEFORE and per statement, so the marker precedes the transaction's rows in
-- the WAL and costs one probe per statement rather than one per row. SECURITY
-- DEFINER because no app role holds a grant on the table, and the owner (the
-- migration superuser) is outside the floor.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mecha.mark_txn() RETURNS trigger
  LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER
  SET search_path = pg_catalog
  AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO mecha.txn_trace (txid, traceparent)
    VALUES (pg_current_xact_id()::text::bigint, mecha.traceparent())
    ON CONFLICT (txid) DO NOTHING;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;

if [ -n "$BUILDKIT_SYNTAX" ]; then

s=0

docker compose -p "$p" --profile '*' -f "$f" down -v --timeout 0 --remove-orphans
exit "$s"

        end

    end

COPY <<'CDCTRACE' /cdc-trace.yaml
# The change feed's transaction trace, joined onto every row: shared by every
# stream reading cdc-events through the transform's `-r`, since streams mode
# refuses resources in a stream's own file.
#
# A writing transaction's first change on the bus is its marker
# (mecha.txn_trace, rls.sql), and conduit does not interleave transactions, so
# the marker last read is the transaction of every row after it. A row's own
# txid cannot answer instead: the bus spells a delete as its before-image,
# indistinguishable from an insert, and that image's txid, where it carries
# more than its key, is its last writer's.
#
# A stream runs this among its INPUT processors, which Connect runs on one
# goroutine whatever the pipeline's threads, after stamping @cdc_consumer with
# a name no other stream uses: the cache is one per process, and each stream
# reads the bus at its own position. The marker is consumed and dropped; a
# row leaves with @traceparent set to its transaction's trace, or unset when
# the transaction had none or began before this process read its marker.
cache_resources:
  - label: cdc_trace
    memory:
      # One entry per stream, replaced by every marker: the TTL bounds nothing
      # and only has to outlast the longest transaction's rows (the default
      # is 5m).
      default_ttl: 24h

processor_resources:
  - label: cdc_trace_join
    # A batch runs each processor over every message before the next, so a
    # marker mid-batch would reach the rows after it only once the batch had
    # already read the cache; for_each runs the batch a message at a time.
    for_each:
      - switch:
          - check: '@cdc_consumer.or("") == ""'
            processors:
              - crash: a cdc-events stream ran cdc_trace_join without stamping @cdc_consumer
          - check: this.catch({}).data.or("").catch("").parse_json().catch({}).__table.or("") == "txn_trace"
            processors:
              # A marker without its NOT NULL trace keeps the error and stays
              # on the stream, where the consumer refuses it as it would any
              # malformed row.
              - try:
                  - mapping: |
                      let trace = this.data.parse_json().traceparent
                      root = if $trace.type() == "string" { $trace } else { throw("txn_trace marker has no traceparent") }
                  - cache:
                      resource: cdc_trace
                      operator: set
                      key: ${! @cdc_consumer }
                      value: ${! content() }
                  - mapping: root = deleted()
          - processors:
              - branch:
                  request_map: root = ""
                  processors:
                    - cache:
                        resource: cdc_trace
                        operator: get
                        key: ${! @cdc_consumer }
                    # No marker read yet: the transaction's trace is unknown.
                    - catch:
                        - mapping: root = ""
                  result_map: meta traceparent = if content().string() != "" { content().string() } else { deleted() }

  # A coalesced call's @traceparent, over a batch archived as a JSON array whose
  # elements carry their row's @traceparent as `trace` (archive keeps no
  # metadata): the first transaction's trace, the one that set the call off.
  - label: cdc_trace_batch
    mutation: |
      let traces = this.map_each(m -> m.trace).filter(t -> t != "")
      meta traceparent = if $traces.length() > 0 { $traces.index(0) } else { deleted() }

CDCTRACE
